headline: Moss genomics and algal phylogenomics probe the origins of land plant lineages
label: Bryophyte And Algal Genomics
summary: New moss genome and sex-chromosome preprints pair with a phylogenomic study of land plant algal relatives.
synthesis: The dominant thread is expanded genomic sampling of non-model photosynthetic lineages at the base of the land plant tree. The Warnstorfia fluitans preprint reports a 725 Mb de novo moss assembly with 30,421 predicted genes and chloroplast and mitochondrial genomes. A second preprint examines U/V sex chromosomes in Polytrichaceae mosses, reporting slow expansion of recombination suppression on ancient sex chromosomes in a haploid life cycle context. The published zygnematophycean study is phylogenomic, analyzing 104 transcriptomes (43 newly sequenced) across 2243 loci to resolve deep genetic structure and ancient radiations among the closest algal relatives of land plants. The assembly and sex-chromosome preprints carry this thread directly, while the published study supplies comparative framing. What is new is the pairing of organellar genomes with nuclear assemblies and of lineage-level sampling with phylogenetic context.
